records.label: Patients with onset <7 years and milder course

phenotypes.text: cystinosis with milder course than infantile nephropathic form

quotes: For three patients, the age of onset of cystinosis was <7 years but the course of the disease was milder than the infantile nephropathic form.
This suggests that the missense mutations found in these individuals allow production of functional protein

records.label: Infantile nephropathic cystinosis patients
quotes: Out of 25 patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, 12 have two severely truncating mutations, which is consistent with a loss of functional protein, and 13 have missense or in-frame deletions, which would result in disruption of transmembrane domains and loss of protein function.

notes.statement: Macías-Vidal et al. (2009) analyzed the CTNS gene in 32 patients with cystinosis from Spain.
quotes: Analysis of the CTNS gene in 32 cystinosis patients from Spain.

notes.statement: Attard et al. (1999) found 23 different CTNS mutations (14 novel) in patients with infantile nephropathic, late-onset, and atypical cystinosis. Infantile patients had 2 severely truncating mutations or missense/in-frame deletions predicted to disrupt transmembrane domains, whereas mutations in 2 late-onset patients affected functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin, accounting for their milder phenotype.
quotes: We found 23 different mutations in CTNS; 14 are novel mutations.
Mutations found in two late-onset patients affect functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin, which accounts for their milder phenotype.

notes.statement: Attard et al. (1999) described late-onset cystinosis as a rarer form of the disorder, with symptoms beginning between 12 and 15 years of age.
quotes: Late-onset cystinosis, a rarer form of the disorder, is characterized by onset of symptoms between 12 and 15 years of age.

notes.statement: Thoene et al. (1999) studied 6 patients with intermediate cystinosis and found CTNS mutations, 2 of them not previously described. The disease resulted either from one mild mutation combined with one mutation known to cause nephropathic cystinosis, or from homozygosity for a mutation predicted to be mild.
quotes: Six patients with the intermediate form of cystinosis are described. Two have new mutations not previously described.
The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.

notes.statement: Thoene et al. (1999) showed that transfecting cystinotic fibroblasts with either normal CTNS cDNA or a cDNA carrying a mutation that causes intermediate cystinosis partially corrected the cells' phenotype.
quotes: Partial phenotypic correction of cystinotic fibroblasts by transfection with normal cDNA or a cDNA derived from a mutation causing intermediate cystinosis is demonstrated.

notes.statement: Spear et al. (1971) reported polykaryocytosis (multinucleated cells) of the visceral glomerular epithelium in cystinosis and described an unusual clinical variant of the disorder.
quotes: Polykaryocytosis of the visceral glomerular epithelium in cystinosis with description of an unusual clinical variant.

notes.statement: Goldman et al. (1971) described adolescent cystinosis and compared it with the infantile and adult forms of cystinosis.
quotes: Adolescent cystinosis: comparisons with infantile and adult forms.
